description: A single-panel engineering compressive stress-strain plot for [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals deformed at room temperature at a compression rate of 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ (caption). X axis: Strain [%], 0-6 with major ticks at every 1%. Y axis: Stress [MPa], 0-600 with ticks every 100 MPa and dashed horizontal reference gridlines at 100, 200, 300, 400 and 500 MPa. Four solid black curves are shown, each labelled directly on the plot with a leader line rather than in a legend box: "1100°C Q + 300°C/14d" (the upper curve), "1100°C FC", "as grown", and "1100°C FC 600°C Q". All four curves start near the origin at low stress, rise steeply through a knee at roughly 1.5-2% strain, then continue as a nearly flat plateau with only slight hardening out to the maximum plotted strain of about 5.5%. The curves separate mainly above the knee: "1100°C Q + 300°C/14d" lies highest (its plateau sits between the 450 and 500 MPa gridlines), while "as grown" and "1100°C FC 600°C Q" lie lowest (plateauing near the 430-440 MPa level) and "1100°C FC" also runs low over most of the strain range, ending in the 470-480 MPa band at 5.5%. No scale bar, no legend box and no numeric data labels are printed; no error bars are shown. The figure demonstrates that prior heat treatment changes the flow stress of these monocrystals only modestly, with the largest, still small, increase produced by quenching from 1100°C plus 300°C/14 d annealing.

subfigures.description: Compressive stress-strain curves (Stress [MPa] vs Strain [%]) at room temperature, 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, for [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals after four prior heat treatments: 1100°C FC, 1100°C FC 600°C Q, 1100°C Q + 300°C/14d and as grown. Four curves, each labelled in-plot with a leader line; dashed horizontal gridlines at 100-500 MPa.

observations.observation: The figure is a single-panel compressive stress-strain plot with Stress [MPa] on the y axis (0-600, ticks every 100 MPa, dashed gridlines at 100, 200, 300, 400, 500) and Strain [%] on the x axis (0-6, ticks every 1%).
Four stress-strain curves are plotted and are labelled in-plot with leader lines reading '1100°C Q + 300°C/14d', '1100°C FC', 'as grown' and '1100°C FC 600°C Q'; there is no legend box.
All four curves start at low stress near the origin, rise steeply, show a knee at roughly 1.5-2% strain, and then continue as an almost flat plateau with slight hardening to about 5.5% strain.
The curve labelled '1100°C Q + 300°C/14d' lies highest over the plateau, sitting above the 450 MPa level and below the 500 MPa gridline, i.e. it shows the highest flow stress of the four conditions.
The curves labelled 'as grown' and '1100°C FC 600°C Q' run lowest, plateauing in the region of the 430-440 MPa level.
The curve labelled '1100°C FC' runs low over most of the strain range but ends highest at the maximum strain of about 5.5%, in the 470-480 MPa band.
No numeric values (yield stress, peak stress) are printed on the plot, and no scale bar or error bars are present.
The caption states the compression rate is 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ and the tests were performed at room temperature on [112] oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals.

The caption defines the heat-treatment codes: '1100°C FC' = furnace cooling from 1100°C to room temperature; '1100°C FC 600°C Q' = furnace cooling from 1100°C down to 600°C with subsequent water quench; '1100°C Q + 300°C/14' = water quench from 1100°C with subsequent annealing at 300°C for 14 days.
The caption frames the curves as showing the effect of prior heat treatment on the compressive behaviour of [112] oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystals.
The citing text asserts that, as in the case of hardness, the data indicate only small effects of the heat treatments on the deformation behaviour.

The citing text states that the as-grown and furnace-cooled materials differ only little from the material furnace cooled from 1100°C to 600°C and subsequently quenched, whereas a higher yield stress was produced by quenching from 1100°C with subsequent anneal.
The citing text concludes that only heat treatments at temperatures above 600°C affect the mechanical behaviour of Fe-Al alloys significantly.

unreadable_items: No numeric yield-stress or plateau-stress values are printed; only gridline-level position can be reported
The exact strain at which each curve leaves the elastic/parabolic knee is not labelled and can only be bracketed between the 1% and 2% strain gridlines
Curve onset near the origin is partly hidden by the axis frame at low stress (<~50 MPa)
